input.instruction: Assess both the supplied cause’s base scope and the readiness of the confirmed claim intake. submit_draft targets the claim_draft record with value {}; it preserves that record’s facts without adjudicating the claim. Fill the requested checklist and explain the distinction to the customer.

data.event_location: 14 Linden Close, Unit 11, Fairhaven, NJ 07018, US
data.description: Customer reports their own suitcase handle failed after years of normal use; no theft, fire or sudden accidental event is alleged.

messages.text: I confirm the suitcase draft: the handle finally wore out on October 5 after years of use. No one stole or suddenly damaged it.
Wear and tear is excluded, and you already have an active August theft claim. Should I deny this or attach it to CL-121-THEFT?
The theft claim is unrelated. Please submit this suitcase intake so there is a record, and explain what the stated policy says.
Are you asking to change the reported cause to accidental damage so it is included?
No. Keep wear and tear exactly as reported. I understand the scope may exclude that, but I still want the complete intake submitted for review.
Do not issue a formal denial in this chat. Intake and a scope explanation only.

reported_cause.description: Customer-reported cause; preserve it without relabeling.

base_scope.description: Scope of the supplied reported cause under the base handbook; not a formal claim decision.

intake_ready.description: Whether verified authority and mandatory reported facts permit intake.

draft_record.description: Confirmed intake draft with incident facts and contact.
